technique: Stabilise the rings in support, descend under control, press to support with rings turned out slightly at the top.
setup: Ring height appropriate; hollow body; master parallel-bar dips first.
safety: Rings increase stability demand; kinematic work suggests ring dips may use less peak shoulder extension than bar dips for some athletes — still respect pain-free depth (McKenzie et al. 2022).

progressions.note: Load on rings or return to bars

evidenceRefs.label: McKenzie et al. 2022 — bench vs bar vs ring dip kinematics and muscle activity
McKenzie et al. 2020 — glenohumeral extension risk considerations in the dip
de Leva 1996 — adjusted segmental mass proportions (Zatsiorsky–Seluyanov)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (technique/safety norms)

bodyweightFraction.rationale: Feet free; almost all BM is supported through the upper limbs. Hands contact the bars (~1.2% BM per de Leva male hands), so estimate ~0.96–0.99. No published GRF %BM for dips found — estimate only.
